text:
Clayton Keller has 24 points in 18 games and 19 of them are assists. He is on a five-game point streak with eight helpers in it, including three in a win in Toronto. That is who he is now: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile of forwards in primary shot assists last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among all forwards in wins above replacement.

Two things to keep an eye on. First, 16 of his 24 points have come on the power play, and his scoring rate of 4.34 points per 60 is well above our range for him (about 2.95 to 3.81). Second, Utah gets only 49% of the expected goals with him on at five-on-five and is better by that measure when he sits. The power play is carrying his line.

His own shooting is a touch cold at 10.6%, so the goals should tick up even as the assists cool. Our projection lands him around 95 points, which would be a career year.
headline: Keller is setting up everybody in Utah
